topics.label: Course and Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, course structure, and key learning objectives concerning cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by contrasting intrinsic biological errors with environmental risks and examining global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens drive malignancy, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of infectious synergy and genetic translocation.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical agents and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA adducts, damage, and mutational transversions.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Multi-Stage Carcinogenesis Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters and chronic inflammatory agents from mutational initiators using experimental models and asbestos pathology.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility, Developmental Timing, and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cellular proliferative states across host life stages modulate susceptibility to carcinogens and summarize the mechanistic causes of cancer.

topics.label: Methods for Determining Carcinogenicity and Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity alongside considerations of exposure risk and benefit.
